means: Borrowed from live-action film: dramatic lighting, shallow depth, considered framing, wide aspect. It names a QUALITY, not a thing in the picture.
does: On this box, close to nothing you can point at. studio/effects.json records the measured rule for the prompt tier - tags that name a THING (locker room, number 7, floodlights) land reliably, tags that name a QUALITY (night, cold, exhausted, melancholy) frequently do not - and 'cinematic' is squarely the second kind. It sits in the house style of every film here and is not the reason those films look cinematic: the deterministic grade in short.py and the explicit camera and lighting tags are.
reach_for_it: rarely on its own. If you want the cinematic look, name it - 'from below', 'dynamic angle', 'floodlights', 'backlighting', 'depth of field' - or move it out of the prompt entirely and into the grade, which is exactly what this project did with the look variable after finding the prompt half inert.
used_in: the house style tag of every film here, where it is largely inherited habit - see studio/looks/*.json for the deterministic version of the same intent
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
